title: National rollout of Photos at Test

content.text: Earlier this year we completed phase 2 of the MOT Photos at Test trial, formerly known as Images in Garages. Phase 2 of the trial was really important because it showed that we’d progressed to a point where national rollout is now possible.
Why we’re introducing photos at test
Although rare, MOT fraud compromises road safety and damages the reputation of hard working MOT testers across the country.
We’re introducing photos at test to:
Results of the trials
Across phases 1 and 2 of the trials, over 300 garages took part, uploading over 60,000 images to MTS with a 92% success rate.
The trials also demonstrated that the feature had minimal impact on testing times, with initial tests remaining at around 40 minutes and retests only slightly longer.
We were also pleased to see that 88% those involved in the trial were ‘very satisfied’ or ‘satisfied’ with how easy the new feature was to use.
Overall, the trials were a success and demonstrated how well testers adapted to including a photo of the vehicle being tested in the testing bay.
Next steps
On 3 August 2026, the national rollout began and an additional 2,500 garages across Great Britain received access to the feature.
Over time we will provide access to more garages until all MOT testers have access to upload photos.
We’d recommend using the new feature once it becomes available to your garage. Familiarise yourself with how it works, as it may become mandatory in future.
How to take a photo of the test
You’ll see the new feature on the test registration process once your garage is given access:
On a desktop
Scan the QR code shown during the vehicle registration process using a device with a camera and internet connection, such as a phone or tablet.
Take the photo of the vehicle in the testing bay. The image will automatically upload to MTS.
With a phone or tablet
During vehicle registration, you can upload an image of the vehicle on the testing equipment directly.
Take the photo of the vehicle in the testing bay. The image will upload directly to MTS.
